Dots are agents. The highlighted agent has a numbered marker, route and goal ring. Agents can wait; they cannot share a cell or swap across an edge.
Travel cost excludes steps spent staying at a goal. Final arrival time includes any later departures and returns.

Round two improved the local archive on all 12 cases. Random repair won development selection; no generally superior new method was established. These are discrete benchmark paths, not validated robot trajectories.

Evidence for this view

Repair comparisons share frozen starting plans and search-state limits. LaCAM3 wall-deadline runs provide context; they are not equal-compute comparisons. The two named repair views use seed 101. The archive view shows the best observed primary-cost witness across all recorded runs, not a single-policy result.

Contains information from Moving AI Lab benchmarks, available under the ODC Attribution License. Baseline solver: LaCAM3 · Keisuke Okumura. Sturtevant, “Benchmarks for Grid-Based Pathfinding,” 2012.
